synopsis: ISO 21448:2022 (SOTIF) addresses harm from perception or performance insufficiencies without component failure, but it is a road-vehicle standard and does not apply by scope to the booklet’s heavy off-road collision-mitigation system [f15292, f2355, f12065]. The booklet nevertheless recommends borrowing its triggering-condition logic and assurance structure for perception, scenario engineering and the safety case, rather than presenting it as automatically governing the machine [f654, f12264, f15309, f8945]. Phase 0 should use these concepts when defining the ODD, hazards, scenarios and acceptance metrics; for a team starting in October 2026, a safety-case skeleton using perception concepts from ISO 21448 is considered realistic by mid-2027 [f707, f829]. The glossary explains functional insufficiencies, triggering conditions such as glare and dust, and four situation areas: known safe, known unsafe, unknown unsafe and unknown safe [f12009, f12010, f12011]. Reliance remains qualified: several chapters report that the standard, its simulation provisions and tool-acceptance rules were not verified, while the brake/perception allocation cites draft evidence and Chapter 12 labels its perception-gap reference as on-road evidence [f4336, f8942, f8155, f6580, f10339].
